description: Blue rectangular plate carrying a white hooked U-turn arrow, marking a highway U-turn gap or bridge.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Slim galvanised post carrying a flat upright rectangular plate near the top, plate face solid blue with a thin white border inset from the edge, a bold white hooked arrow curving back on itself filling the upper part of the plate, white lettering below it reading the Thai line กลับรถ above a smaller roman line reading U-TURN, plate mounted square across the post Materials: Blue retroreflective sheeting dulled and chalky on the sun-facing side, white pictogram and border paint chipped at the plate corners, galvanised post with rust at the ground line, road spatter across the lower face.

Legend: this object is a SIGN, and its printed legend is part of the object, not an annotation on the photograph. Render every letter, numeral, pictogram, arrow and coloured band described above, exactly as described and nothing more. Thai script must be rendered as Thai script with correct glyph shapes, above the roman line where both are described. Lettering and pictograms lie flat on the sign face, sharp, high-contrast and correctly proportioned, and the face must stay legible despite the camera angle. Do not leave the face blank, do not substitute lorem or invented wording, and do not add any text that was not described.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no watermarks, no drop shadow, and no border around the photograph itself.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.92 -- the five layers mean 0.904 and the four critical features 0.915. 248/800 triangles, 2/2 draw calls, 2/2 materials, 2/2 unique geometries, one 21.8 KB baked atlas and one 512 px canvas (2.9 MB texture VRAM), 68 ms to construct.

featureReviews.evidence: Rounded tray 0.9 x 1.2 m (r 0.045) 33 mm deep with a 20 mm rim lip 8 mm proud, tinted #e6e9eb against the plate's bright edge return; corners and the white rule inset 0.025 m at 0.022 m wide read off rows 400 and column 430 of the plate. Bounds 0.9 x 2.4 x 0.146 m against the corrected declaration 0.9 x 2.4 x 0.14.
featureReviews.notes: The near-edge return in the plate is thicker than the 33 mm tray at the corner where the camera looks along it; a thicker tray would put the face further from the post than the plate's bracket shadow allows.

featureReviews.evidence: Post 0.09 m square: the plate reads 48 px across two faces against a 416 px near plate edge of 1.2 m (0.138 m visible, 0.09-0.10 m square) and the proxy 4 of 24 plate-width columns; the first build's 0.05 m post read as wire. The plate sits on two 0.56 m channel brackets and a spine 12 mm behind the tray, so at 90/270 nothing shows through (holeviz: 0 enclosed pixels at all four azimuths).
featureReviews.notes: The post's ground contact is not in the plate; the 2.3 m post top behind the plate is the assembly convention, not an observation.

featureReviews.evidence: The face IS the plate: its printed field homography-rectified from corners (401,179) (652,101) (631,494) (416,595) into a 512 x 683 image (scratch/_signage/v2/rectify.py), pasted inside a drawn blue margin and white rule at 512 px/m (atlas.py, 21.8 KB WebP), and sampled planarly by the tray's +Z face. Arrow hooks left, Thai over Latin, grime and fading at the plate's own positions; the 000 frame shows the legend unmirrored.
featureReviews.notes: Rectified from ~250 plate pixels across, so the lettering edge is the plate's softness, not a vector's.

featureReviews.evidence: Height-keyed paint canvas over 2.4 m: rust hband at v 0.452-0.50 (the 0.12 m the plate reads under the bottom edge, #664d39..#87674e) with 36 streaks hanging from it, a ground band and a mud axis tint (#a89070) over 0.03-0.32 m, zinc base authored #c7ccd1 for the harness's 0.6x side-lit transfer so the post returns luma 133 at 0 against the plate's 121. Foot renders #57432e / #493928 at 0 / 180 (sat 0.45-0.47), outside the gate window on chroma.
featureReviews.notes: The plate's post is a brighter, more mottled spangle than the canvas's drift gives; the rim lip is tinted rather than carrying the plate's corner rust drip.
